title-tag: Refinishing Hickory Floors in Sammamish: A Species Guide
meta-description: Hickory is the hardest domestic floor wood (1,820 Janka) and the blotchiest to stain. A Sammamish contractor on sanding it flat and finishing it right.
post-summary: October 26, 2026 · Hickory is the hardest domestic floor species (1,820 Janka vs red oak’s 1,290), its shifting density pushes sanders around, and its calico grain makes stain blotch like nothing else. Why the plateau’s favorite hardwood needs a disciplined crew — and why natural finish at $3.99/sq ft is usually the right answer.
